frozen_original.synopsis: During New York's civil fraud trial, prosecutors presented evidence that Trump Organization executives engaged in a scheme of double-billing expenses by routing them through internal intercompany loans that were never repaid. The practice artificially inflated the profitability of certain properties while hiding expenses that would reduce asset valuations. The double-billing scheme was systematic enough that Judge Arthur Engoron found it to be a deliberate pattern rather than accounting error. The findings revealed a corporate culture of deliberate financial manipulation stretching back years across multiple Trump business units. Several Trump Organization executives had previously pleaded guilty to related charges.

proposal.description_long: An Associated Press report from October 11, 2023, describes testimony by a retired bank official at the New York civil-fraud trial brought by Attorney General Letitia James against Donald Trump, his company, and top executives. The official testified that Trump’s financial statements were key to the bank’s approval of a $125 million loan in 2011 for Trump’s Doral golf resort in Florida and a $107 million loan in 2012 for his Chicago hotel and tower. AP reported that this was the first time a bank official testified in court about the statements’ effect on Trump’s ability to obtain loans. The trial concerned whether financial statements used for lending were fraudulent, but this testimony does not establish that expenses were billed twice through internal loans. The supplied article and prior notes do not identify a duplicated expense, an internal-loan transaction, or a judicial finding on that alleged mechanism. The title is narrowed to the specific lending testimony the cited report supports.
